T1_replay_erasure.statement: For handlers whose transition depends only on the set of stable logical vote keys, deleting replay copies preserves state, quorum, and every state-based safety observation.

T2_local_closure_lifting.statement: If closure-added messages are R-increasing, every original transition is forward-simulated by R, and the unsafe predicate is upward closed under R, then inserting any finite sequence of closure-added messages while preserving the order of original messages preserves unsafety.

T3_phase_coupled_separation.statement: For n=3f+1 and q=2f+1, if the unique honest quorum-intersection pivot must receive enabling evidence E and a later repair/terminal message R shares the same directed edge, then a type-uniform view graph cannot both form the first quorum and keep the pivot available for a conflicting quorum. A phase-specific schedule can deliver E while omitting R; bounded late delivery can defer R past round two.

T4_bounded_terminal_delay.statement: When the only coupled repair is terminal and can be postponed past the conflicting view without changing other enabling transitions, one-view delay simulates the relevant phase-specific witness.

T5_non_idempotent_replay_separation.statement: Counting message instances instead of stable logical signer keys admits a finite replay trace that reaches a spurious quorum.
